```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Mesmos helpers de report/report_template.rmd e report/monthly_report_template.rmd
# -- ver esses ficheiros para os comentarios completos sobre cada um.
report_table <- function(x, caption = NULL, max_col_width_cm = NULL, col_widths_cm = NULL) {
  ft <- flextable::flextable(round_display(x)) |>
    flextable::theme_box() |>
    flextable::bg(part = "header", bg = "gray85") |>
    flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "header") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "body") |>
    flextable::align(align = "center", part = "header") |>
    flextable::valign(valign = "center", part = "all") |>
    flextable::autofit()
  if (!is.null(max_col_width_cm)) ft <- cap_col_width(ft, max_col_width_cm)
  if (!is.null(col_widths_cm)) ft <- set_col_max_width(ft, col_widths_cm)
  if (!is.null(caption)) ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft, caption)
  ft
}

round_display <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  for (col in names(x)) {
    v <- x[[col]]
    if (!is.numeric(v) || is.integer(v)) next
    if (all(v == round(v), na.rm = TRUE)) next
    x[[col]] <- vapply(v, function(val) {
      if (is.na(val)) return(NA_character_)
      d <- digits
      while (round(val, d) == 0 && val != 0 && d < 6) d <- d + 1
      sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), val)
    }, character(1))
  }
  x
}

cap_col_width <- function(ft, max_width_cm = 2) {
  widths_in <- dim(ft)$widths
  capped_cm <- pmin(widths_in * 2.54, max_width_cm)
  flextable::width(ft, j = seq_along(capped_cm), width = capped_cm, unit = "cm")
}

set_col_max_width <- function(ft, widths_cm) {
  widths_in <- dim(ft)$widths
  idx <- match(names(widths_cm), ft$col_keys)
  hit <- !is.na(idx)
  if (any(hit)) {
    capped_cm <- pmin(widths_in[idx[hit]] * 2.54, unname(widths_cm[hit]))
    ft <- flextable::width(ft, j = idx[hit], width = capped_cm, unit = "cm")
  }
  ft
}

rename_display <- function(x, mapping) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  idx <- match(names(mapping), names(x))
  hit <- !is.na(idx)
  names(x)[idx[hit]] <- unname(mapping)[hit]
  x
}

annex_note <- function(xlsx_name) {
  if (!is.null(xlsx_name)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n*The full table is available in the accompanying workbook: `%s`.*\n", xlsx_name))
  }
}
```

# Context and Purpose

Dzhankeldy (DGY) is monitored by only `r params$n_idf_dgy` IdentiFlight (IDF) units, covering a limited subset of its `r params$n_turbines_dgy` turbines -- a monitoring history too short and too narrow, on its own, to directly support a request to restore normal (non-curtailed) operation. Bash (BSH), approximately 50 km away, shares the same avian community and the same priority species (see the list below), and has an extensive monitoring history across detections, terrain, curtailment response and topography.

This note builds an indirect, comparison-based case for DGY: where BSH shows a stable, well-characterised pattern, and DGY -- despite its limited own history -- shows a consistent pattern with BSH, that consistency itself is evidence that DGY's bird activity and risk profile is not meaningfully different from BSH's.

Two lines of evidence are presented below: (1) the weekly seasonal presence of priority species from track data, and (2) topography and the associated seasonal pattern of space use. A third line of evidence, a raptor breeding survey conducted at DGY, is planned for a future revision of this note (see placeholder section below).

Priority species considered in this comparison (union of both farms' priority lists): `r params$priority_species_compare`.

<!-- Source: import_farm_data(), explore_bsh_dgy_comparison.R -->

# Weekly Presence of Priority Species (Track Data)

For each priority species, presence is scored 0/1 per 7-day week over the comparison window above -- 1 if at least one track of that species was detected in that week, 0 otherwise. Week bins are anchored to the same start date in both farms (not to each farm's own start of data), so that week N refers to the same calendar dates in BSH and DGY. For each species, the BSH and DGY rows are shown one above the other, in distinct colours, so that the two farms can be compared directly on a like-for-like seasonal basis. The comparison window itself is bounded by DGY's shorter history (the intersection of both farms' available periods).

<!-- Source: plot_species_presence_heatmap(), explore_bsh_dgy_comparison.R -->
```{r species-presence-plot, fig.width=6.30, fig.height=7}
if (!is.null(params$species_presence_plot)) print(params$species_presence_plot)
```

The table below summarises, per species, the percentage of weeks in the comparison window with at least one detection in each farm -- a similar percentage between farms, for a given species, indicates a similar seasonal presence pattern despite DGY's shorter own history.

## Track Intensity per IDF Unit

For the same species as in the presence plot above, the number of distinct tracks per week is divided by the number of days in that week and by the number of IDF units of the farm (`r params$n_idf_bsh` in BSH, `r params$n_idf_dgy` in DGY), giving the mean number of tracks per day per IDF unit. This normalisation controls for the difference in the number of IDF units between the two farms. The layout follows the presence plot: one panel per species, with BSH and DGY in distinct colours, one above the other, on the same weekly axis. Colour intensity is proportional to the weekly value, relative to the maximum weekly value of each row (species and farm), so that the temporal dynamics of each row stand out; weeks with no tracks are shown in dark grey. Absolute values are given in the table below.

# Topography and Seasonal Space-Use Comparison

Each turbine's surrounding terrain is classified as ridge, complex or flat from a digital elevation model (DEM), using the same methodology applied in the annual report (turbine elevation relative to its surroundings, and local ground slope -- see `R/turbine_terrain_classification.R`). DGY has its own DEM, so this classification -- and the associated weekly pattern of space use by terrain class (`R/track_terrain_temporal.R`) -- is computed independently for each farm, not inferred from BSH alone. The comparison below checks whether the two farms present a similar terrain profile and a similar seasonal relationship between terrain class and bird activity; where they do, BSH's better-characterised pattern (from its longer track history) becomes a reasonable proxy for what DGY's own pattern is likely to be, even where DGY's own history is too short to establish it directly.

<!-- Source: summarise_terrain_class_counts(), R/turbine_terrain_classification.R -->

## Terrain Classification Maps

<!-- Source: plot_turbine_terrain_map(), R/turbine_terrain_classification.R -->
```{r terrain-map-helper, include=FALSE}
# Mapas a 7 x 7 cm (2.76 in): texto e pontos reduzidos (size = 3 por omissao em
# plot_turbine_terrain_map()), legenda por baixo.
shrink_map <- function(p, title) {
  for (i in seq_along(p$layers)) {
    if (identical(p$layers[[i]]$aes_params$size, 3)) p$layers[[i]]$aes_params$size <- 1.2
  }
  p + ggplot2::labs(title = title) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6),
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 5),
      legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6),
      legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6),
      legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"),
      legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
    )
}
```
```{r terrain-map-bsh, fig.width=2.756, fig.height=2.756}

```

# Raptor Breeding Survey (BSH and DGY)

The data in this section were extracted from the report *Breeding Raptor Nest Monitoring 2026* (Bash WPP and Dzhankeldy WPP), which covers both farms. All species recorded in that report are included: every nest with an identified species (active or inactive) in the nest inventories, and the Common Kestrel nests on the Bash overhead transmission line (OHTL) pylons. Breeding outcome is the classification given in the survey report (successful, failed, not started or unknown); nest-to-turbine distances are those reported for occupied nests.

<!-- Source: Nest_inventory / Breeding_success / Pylon_kestrel_nests, inputs/breeding_survey_2026.xlsx -->

# Summary and Recommendation

*This section will be completed once the raptor breeding survey evidence above is available. Provisionally, based on the two lines of evidence presented (seasonal presence of priority species, and topography-linked space use), it is expected that DGY's bird activity and risk profile can be characterised as consistent with BSH's -- a comparison to be confirmed and finalised, with the specific operational recommendation, once the full evidence base is assembled.*
